## Dataset "Gotchas"

There are a few known tricky aspects to the dataset; some are artifacts of the data collection process, others are the result of minor issues in our ETL process.

### Data Dictionary Naming Quirks

There are a few fields that are named slightly differently between the [CSV data dictionary](https://github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-redcap/blob/main/data/bridge2ai_voice_project_data_dictionary.csv) and the released TSV files on PhysioNet.
Some (most?) of the "gold-standard diagnosis" columns use a `_gsd` suffix in the CSV data dictionary, but in the corresponding TSV file (and accompanying JSON data dictionary) use a `_gold_standard_diagnosis` suffix.

For example, the CSV lists a column in the airway stenosis diagnosis file named `diagnosis_as_gsd`, but in the file itself it is named `diagnosis_as_gold_standard_diagnosis`.

### TSV File Column Order

The TSV files have their columns in _alphabetical order_, not in the order that they appear in the full CSV data dictionary, which lists fields in the order that they appeared in their associated RedCap data collection instruments.

### Let's talk about sex

There are two columns attempting to capture information about participant's sex at birth; the details are a very long story, but the one you _probably_ want to use is `sex_at_birth`. See below for a cross-tabulation of what is in the actual dataset:



```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE,message=FALSE}

library(tidyverse)
library(gt)
library(gtsummary)
source("ingest.R")

PATH_TO_PHYSIONET_DOWNLOAD_DIR <- "/Users/bedricks/Documents/b2ai_3.1/adult"

PHENOTYPES_DIR <- fs::path_join(c(PATH_TO_PHYSIONET_DOWNLOAD_DIR, "phenotype"))

demographics <- read_tsv(
  fs::path_join(c(
    PHENOTYPES_DIR, "demographics", "demographics.tsv")), col_types=cols(participant_id=col_character())) %>% 
  clean_age_col() # handle age binning

demographics %>% 
  select(sex_at_birth, sex_assigned_at_birth) %>% 
  group_by(sex_at_birth, sex_assigned_at_birth) %>% 
  tally() %>% ungroup() %>% gt %>% sub_missing(missing_text = md("_NA_"))
 
```
